title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Board agreed to retain Charleston Engineering as the Village’s Engineering firm, Kapper & Company as Village Auditors, and Lawyer Bart Zuber as Village Attorney, for the 2026 fiscal year.

Mayor Brad Kessler reported on an ongoing nuisance property located on W. North Avenue.  He stated that he has consulted with the Village Attorney regarding steps needed to move the case forward.  The nuisance issue has persisted for approximately two years, with temporary compliance occurring prior to court dates, followed by recurring violations.  The Village Attorney will address this matter further at the upcoming court hearing.

The next regular meeting has been moved from Monday, May 25th to the following night, due to the observance of Memorial Day.

title: INJURED IN ACCIDENT
full_story:
18-year-old Brent Shroyer of Louisville was injured in a single-vehicle crash late Tuesday night in Effingham County.

Effingham County Sheriff’s Office reports that Shroyer was traveling south on US Highway 45 at 11:50 pm when Shroyer fell asleep.  Shroyer’s vehicle left the roadway to the left, struck an Ameren power pole, and continued traveling south until coming to rest.

Shroyer was taken by Rural Med EMS to St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital in Effingham for treatment.  No citations were issued.

title: SCAM WARNING
full_story:
The Richland County Sheriff’s Office is warning residents about scammers targeting families of people who have been arrested.

The sheriff’s office said scammers are calling family members and telling them they need to send money to get their loved one released from jail on an ankle monitor or placed on pre-trial release.

The callers are demanding as much as $1,175 and telling victims they’ll get the money back minus a $75 fee.

The sheriff’s office said people who receive these calls should not send money, should not provide personal information and should hang up immediately.

Anyone who believes they have been targeted by this scam should contact the Richland County Sheriff’s Office.

title: NUTRIENT STEWARDSHIP FIELD DAYS
full_story:
Illinois Farm Bureau’s Nutrient Stewardship Field Days will return this summer, highlighting members’ conservation efforts throughout the state.

“Field days are an important platform for elevating the voices of those implementing unique regenerative practices,” said Bena Pegg, IFB environmental program manager.  “The farmers leading these events are mentors, sharing practical, local knowledge that helps others build more resilient, productive and sustainable operations.”

Pegg told FarmWeek these events remain part of the effort to help Illinois meet its Nutrient Loss Reduction Strategy goals but have grown into much more.  The summer Nutrient Stewardship Field Days, scheduled June through September, and will cover a range of topics, including soil health, field research, livestock integration and regenerative agriculture.

In our area on July 7th, Jasper, Clark, Cumberland and Richland County Farm Bureaus will host a bus tour to Southern Illinois University and Southern FS to learn firsthand from researchers and agronomists.  The program is an all-day event and will include breakfast, lunch and dinner.

And on August 20th, from 6 to 8 pm, Wayne County Farm Bureau will view the Research trials at the Nutrient Loss Inhibitor Demonstration Plot will be discussed.  This year’s trials focus on the effects of nitrogen stabilizers, micronutrients, humic acid and application timing.

IFB’s Nutrient Stewardship Grant Program funds the 2026 Nutrient Stewardship Field Days.  Since 2015, IFB has awarded $1.75 million to support 192 county-led nutrient stewardship projects.  Additionally, the Pollinator Conservation Grant Program, entering its fifth year, has awarded $165,000 for 45 pollinator projects.

Visit bit.ly/IFBFieldDays for event updates, more information about field day locations and RSVP info.

title: RUN FOR THE WALL
full_story:
Riders honoring veterans and POW/MIA service members will pass through Mt. Vernon on Tuesday morning.

The City of Mt. Vernon is welcoming participants in the annual Run For The Wall motorcycle ride as they travel through the community on Tuesday.  Run For The Wall is a cross-country ride honoring veterans, active military personnel, POWs, MIAs, and their families while raising awareness for those still unaccounted for from past wars and conflicts.

The riders are expected to arrive in Mt. Vernon around 10:45 am and will be traveling along Route 15 to the Mt. Vernon Airport for lunch before departing around 12:45 pm.  Residents should expect increased motorcycle traffic and possible temporary delays during that time.

title: BLACK VULTURE DEPREDATION PERMITS
full_story:
Illinois Farm Bureau recently secured statewide black vulture depredation permits through the US Fish and Wildlife Service through December 31st.  Black vultures are known to prey on young livestock and birthing mothers, causing significant injuries and even death.

IFB continues to work with US Department of Agriculture Wildlife Services to issue federal sub-permits to livestock farmers who are experiencing issues with black vultures on their land.  IFB will also continue to work with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) to secure the necessary state permits for farmers seeking approval.

Black vultures, which have a dark gray head and are aggressive, should not be confused with their larger, less aggressive and red-headed relative, the turkey vulture.  Turkey vultures may be found throughout Illinois.  Black vultures live in southern regions but are expanding their range further north, creating depredation problems for farmers.

IFB will issue sub-permits as a benefit to livestock farmers who are experiencing problems with black vultures and assist in securing IDNR’s required permit.  The sub-permit is available to livestock farmers facing depredation of commercial livestock, which includes cattle, horses, sheep, goats and swine.

Approved applicants will be allowed a maximum of three birds, determined after consultation with USDA Wildlife Services. Following the consultation and approval, a state permit will also be provided by IDNR.

Interested livestock producers may request a sub-permit application by Tasha Bunting, IFB director of commodity programs and food systems, at [email protected].

title: BECOME A MASTER GARDENER
full_story:
Are you thinking about improving your gardening knowledge?  One way to do that is through the University of Illinois Extension’s Master Gardener Program.  The deadline to apply for an online spring session is this Saturday, May 16th.

Program Coordinator Sarah Ruth says being a master gardener is the perfect opportunity for someone who wants to expand their knowledge about horticulture.  She says the online classes offer training similar to what you would get in person.

If you are interested, visit extension.illinois.edu/mms. Classes begin June 8th.

title: AVETT BROTHERS AT STATE FAIR
full_story:
The Illinois State Fair is bringing a night of heartfelt lyrics and high-energy folk rock to the Illinois Lottery Grandstand Stage, as four-time GRAMMY Award nominees The Avett Brothers perform on Thursday, August 20th.

Known for their raw emotion, tight harmonies, and genre-blending sound, The Avett Brothers have built a loyal following across the country.  Their 2009 major-label debut I and Love and You launched them into mainstream success, and they’ve continued that momentum with chart-topping releases including The Carpenter and Magpie and the Dandelion, both debuting in the top five on the Billboard 200.

The band’s 2016 album True Sadness marked a career milestone, debuting at #1 on Billboard’s Top Albums chart and earning two GRAMMY nominations.  The journey behind that album was captured in the acclaimed documentary May It Last: A Portrait of The Avett Brothers, co-directed by Judd Apatow and Michael Bonfiglio.

In recent years, the group has continued to evolve creatively.  Their 2019 album Closer Than Together featured the hit single “High Steppin’,” which reached #1 on the Americana Radio Singles chart.  During the pandemic, The Third Gleam debuted at #1 across multiple Billboard charts, with the single “Victory” also topping Americana radio.

In 2024, the band released The Avett Brothers, a self-titled project that reflects their organic songwriting process and continued artistic growth.  That same year, Swept Away, a Broadway musical inspired by their music, debuted to rave reviews, further showcasing their wide-reaching cultural impact.  Inducted into the North Carolina Music Hall of Fame and recipients of a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Americana Music Association, The Avett Brothers remain a driving force in modern American music.

“The Avett Brothers bring an energy and authenticity that will make this a can’t-miss night at the Illinois State Fair,” said Illinois State Fair Manager Rebecca Clark.

Tickets for The Avett Brothers will go on sale Saturday at 10 am via Ticketmaster.  Tier 3 tickets are $58; Tier 2 tickets are $63; Tier 1 tickets are $68; Track tickets are $73; and Blue Ribbon tickets are $123.  A $30 Pre-Show Party ticket is offered as an additional upgrade for all paid concerts.

Mark your calendars for the 2026 Illinois State Fair, August 13th through August 23rd in Springfield.
